[EFFECT]
The day of the week has a categorical, non-monotonic effect on predicted hourly demand. Sunday (day 0) stands out with the strongest negative contribution (around –0.065 in log space), meaning demand is noticeably pulled down on Sundays compared to the weekly average. Demand contributions then rise progressively from Monday through to Friday, which has the highest positive contribution (+0.041) — the clear peak of the week. Saturday is also positive but slightly lower than Friday (+0.020), creating a pattern where mid-to-late weekdays drive more rentals and Sunday is the softest day.

[IMPORTANCE]
`weekday` is ranked **7th out of 9 features** in terms of importance, with a global importance score of 0.024. It has a real but relatively modest influence on demand — far smaller than the leading drivers like the hour of day, temperature, and year, though slightly more influential than wind speed and holiday status.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since Fridays consistently show the highest predicted demand boost and Sundays the largest predicted dip, consider scheduling slightly more bikes and staff availability heading into Friday evenings, and allow for reduced fleet deployment on Sundays to better match anticipated demand patterns.
